intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 (CLCRP2) is caused by compound heterozygous mutation in the SEC24D gene (607186) on chromosome 4q26.

checks.claim: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 (CLCRP2) is caused by compound heterozygous mutation in the SEC24D gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Three individuals from two families affected by a similar skeletal phenotype were each compound heterozygous for two of these mutant alleles
checks.explanation: Compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations cause a syndromic OI; the boy's phenotype resembles Cole-Carpenter syndrome, but the abstract does not name 'Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2'.

checks.claim: The SEC24D gene is located on chromosome 4q26.
checks.evidence_quote: we report three mutant alleles in SEC24D, a gene encoding a component of the COPII complex
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature not stated in the abstract; accepted as restatement.

paragraphs.text: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 is an autosomal recessive disorder (Zhang et al., 2017) that resembles osteogenesis imperfecta. Its main features are bone fragility with multiple fractures, craniofacial malformations, and severely disturbed ossification of the skull (Garbes et al., 2015).

checks.claim: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: We discovered two novel compound SEC24D mutations of autosomal recessive OI patients.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the SEC24D-related disorder as autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta but never uses the name Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2. Equating the two comes from the OMIM framing, not from this abstract.

checks.claim: Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 resembles osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: cause a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta
checks.explanation: Title describes the disorder as a syndromic form of OI.

checks.claim: The main features of Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 include bone fragility with multiple fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: All three displayed a severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures with prenatal onset.
checks.explanation: Multiple fractures reported in all affected individuals.

checks.claim: The main features of Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 include craniofacial malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: The 7-year-old boy had short stature and craniofacial malformations including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing, and down-slanting palpebral fissures.
checks.explanation: Craniofacial malformations described.

checks.claim: The main features of Cole-Carpenter syndrome-2 include severely disturbed ossification of the skull.
checks.evidence_quote: All three displayed a severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures with prenatal onset.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) described a 7-year-old boy whose phenotype most closely resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome. He had craniofacial malformations, severely disturbed ossification of the skull, and multiple fractures, consistent with a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta.

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) described a 7-year-old boy whose phenotype most closely resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: a 7-year-old boy with a phenotype most closely resembling Cole-Carpenter syndrome
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The 7-year-old boy described by Garbes et al. (2015) had craniofacial malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: The 7-year-old boy had short stature and craniofacial malformations including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The 7-year-old boy described by Garbes et al. (2015) had severely disturbed ossification of the skull.
checks.evidence_quote: All three displayed a severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures with prenatal onset.
checks.explanation: The boy is one of the three.

checks.claim: The 7-year-old boy described by Garbes et al. (2015) had multiple fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: All three displayed a severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures with prenatal onset.
checks.explanation: The boy is one of the three.

checks.claim: The phenotype of the 7-year-old boy described by Garbes et al. (2015) was consistent with a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: cause a syndromic form of osteogenesis imperfecta
checks.explanation: Title characterizes the phenotype as syndromic OI.

paragraphs.text: Zhang et al. (2017) described the SEC24D-related disorder as autosomal recessive. Garbes et al. (2015) reported compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations in affected individuals.

checks.claim: Zhang et al. (2017) described the SEC24D-related disorder as autosomal recessive.
checks.evidence_quote: Our study extended both the phenotypic and the genotypic spectrum of the autosomal recessive OI patients with SEC24D mutations.
checks.explanation: The paper explicitly calls the SEC24D-related OI autosomal recessive (it also says 'recessively inherited forms of OI').

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) reported compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations in individuals affected by the SEC24D-related disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Three individuals from two families affected by a similar skeletal phenotype were each compound heterozygous for two of these mutant alleles
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: By exome sequencing in a boy with a Cole-Carpenter-like phenotype, Garbes et al. (2015) found compound heterozygous mutations in the SEC24D gene. SEC24D encodes a component of the COPII machinery, which is involved in protein export from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). The patient's fibroblasts showed procollagen retained in the ER, which was dilated, so procollagen secretion was impaired. Garbes et al. (2015) also reported SEC24D mutations in a further family with a similar osteogenesis imperfecta-like phenotype.

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) performed exome sequencing in a boy with a Cole-Carpenter-like phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: As a result of a whole-exome sequencing study, we report three mutant alleles in SEC24D
checks.explanation: Whole-exome sequencing study identified the mutations.

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) found compound heterozygous mutations in the SEC24D gene in a boy with a Cole-Carpenter-like phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Three individuals from two families affected by a similar skeletal phenotype were each compound heterozygous for two of these mutant alleles
checks.explanation: The boy is among the compound heterozygous individuals.

checks.claim: SEC24D encodes a component of the COPII machinery.
checks.evidence_quote: SEC24D, a gene encoding a component of the COPII complex involved in protein export from the ER
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The COPII machinery is involved in protein export from the endoplasmic reticulum.
checks.evidence_quote: SEC24D, a gene encoding a component of the COPII complex involved in protein export from the ER
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Fibroblasts from the boy with compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations showed procollagen retained in the endoplasmic reticulum.
checks.evidence_quote: Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy of skin fibroblasts of this individual revealed that ER export of procollagen was inefficient and that ER tubules were dilated
checks.explanation: Abstract says ER export was inefficient; retention is implied but not explicitly stated.

checks.claim: The endoplasmic reticulum in fibroblasts from the boy with compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations was dilated.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed that ER export of procollagen was inefficient and that ER tubules were dilated
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Procollagen secretion was impaired in fibroblasts from the boy with compound heterozygous SEC24D mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed that ER export of procollagen was inefficient
checks.explanation: Inefficient ER export equates to impaired secretion.

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) reported SEC24D mutations in a further family with an osteogenesis imperfecta-like phenotype similar to that of the boy with a Cole-Carpenter-like phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: two fetuses initially suspected to have a severe type of osteogenesis imperfecta
checks.explanation: Two families with similar skeletal phenotype; the fetuses were suspected OI.

paragraphs.text: Garbes et al. (2015) referred to the zebrafish mutant 'bulldog' as Sec24d-deficient.

checks.claim: Garbes et al. (2015) referred to the zebrafish mutant 'bulldog' as Sec24d-deficient.
checks.evidence_quote: the Sec24d-deficient fish mutants vbi (medaka) and bulldog (zebrafish)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.
